questions.stem: What is the general formula for alkenes?
questions.explanation: The general formula for alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ. Alkenes have two fewer hydrogen atoms than the equivalent alkane because of the C=C double bond.

questions.stem: What is the functional group in alkenes?
questions.explanation: The functional group in alkenes is the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C). This double bond makes alkenes more reactive than alkanes.

questions.stem: How can you test whether a substance is an alkene?

options.text: Add it to water and see if it dissolves
Add bromine water; it will decolourise from orange to colourless
Heat it and see if it melts

questions.explanation: Alkenes decolourise bromine water (turning it from orange to colourless) because the C=C double bond reacts with bromine in an addition reaction. Alkanes do not decolourise bromine water.

questions.stem: Why are alkenes described as 'unsaturated' hydrocarbons?

options.text: Because they contain a C=C double bond and can add more atoms
Because they have fewer carbon atoms than alkanes
Because they are gases at room temperature

questions.explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated because the C=C double bond can open up to allow more atoms to bond, through addition reactions. They do not contain the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of ethene?
questions.explanation: Ethene has 2 carbon atoms (n=2). Using CₙH₂ₙ: C₂H₂₍₂₎ = C₂H₄. The two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond: H₂C=CH₂.

questions.stem: Why is the smallest alkene ethene (C₂H₄) rather than methene (CH₂)?

options.text: Methene is too small to exist
You need at least two carbon atoms to form a C=C double bond
Carbon can only form single bonds

questions.explanation: A C=C double bond requires two carbon atoms, so the smallest possible alkene must have at least two carbons. Ethene (C₂H₄) is therefore the simplest alkene.

questions.stem: Compared to alkanes with the same number of carbon atoms, alkenes are:

options.text: Less reactive, due to the double bond
More reactive, because the C=C double bond can undergo addition reactions

questions.explanation: Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes because the C=C double bond is a reactive site that readily undergoes addition reactions with substances like bromine, hydrogen, and water.
